claims.claim: TARG is the reference training-free adaptive retrieval GATE and the closest existing instantiation of our tau* layer: from a k=20 draft prefix it computes mean token entropy, a top1/top2 logit-gap margin U_mar=mean exp(-gap/beta) (beta=3, its recommended default), or small-N prefix variance, and retrieves iff U>tau. The threshold is set training-free on a dev set either by tau=F_U^{-1}(1-rho) to hit a target retrieval budget rho, or by max-dev-accuracy.
claims.relevance: Directly instantiates tau* with an explicit dev-calibration recipe (empirical inverse-CDF) that runs on our dev40 with zero GPU.

claims.claim: TARG found that ensembling its signals did NOT consistently beat the best single gate once tau and k are tuned, so it ships single-signal (margin default). This is in tension with the multi-signal literature and is a concrete ablation we can re-test on the speech-omni.
claims.relevance: Tells us multi-signal fusion is NOT a free win; whether fusion helps is an open, testable question on our stack — one of the cleaner Stage-1 directional probes.

claims.claim: TARG headline: Qwen2.5-7B NQ-Open 39.6 EM at 30.4% retrieval vs 38.8 (never) / 37.4 (always); Llama-3.1-8B NQ-Open 57.6 EM at 0.8% retrieval; 70-90% retrieval cut at matched/better accuracy. It relies on a usefulness-calibration assumption (Sec 3.3): there exists tau* with E[Delta|U<=tau*]<=0 and E[Delta|U>tau*]>=0.
claims.relevance: The 'always-retrieve' column is exactly our step-2 mock; TARG shows a gate can match it while also beating 'never' (closed-book) — i.e. the paired win over BOTH our denominators is the documented TARG result pattern.

claims.claim: Entropy alone is insufficient for SAFE selective prediction: no single signal reliably flags incorrect LLM outputs across tasks/models; fusing entropy + margin + semantic entropy + self-consistency into a gate substantially improves the risk-coverage curve. The standard gate-evaluation protocol is risk-coverage curves scored by AURC / E-AURC plus AUROC for correctness classification.
claims.relevance: Justifies a multi-signal gate candidate AND fixes our step-3 gate evaluation protocol: report AURC/E-AURC/AUROC on risk-coverage, not just point accuracy.

claims.claim: CoCoA is a token-level context-vs-parametric GATE using a genuine multi-signal fusion: Renyi(alpha=0.5) divergence between the parametric distribution p_theta (no context) and contextual p_theta^ctx, an entropy gap ΔH, and contextual peakedness m; fused into conflict score s_t=sigmoid(D+gamma·ΔH+delta) and blend weight lambda_t=sigmoid(z·log m_t + logit(1-s_t)), then q ∝ (p_ctx)^lambda (p_theta)^(1-lambda). Hyperparameters are fixed (alpha=0.5,z=5,gamma=1), no per-task training.
claims.relevance: The when-to-inject gate that also instantiates delta_corr: p_theta vs p_theta^ctx are two context-differentiated readings of the same frozen model — exactly our TH2a two-system framing at token granularity.

claims.claim: CoCoA preserves accuracy in LOW-conflict settings where prior contrastive decoding collapses: NQ-SYNTH low-conflict 86.6% (CoCoA) vs 64.0% (CAD, a 24.2-pt drop) vs 88.2 greedy; NQ-SWAP high-conflict 80.8% (+18.0 over AdaCAD). The failure mode it fixes — a static context-trust rule tanking non-conflicting items — is precisely the kNN-Whisper OOD-harm / recall-floor risk we already flagged.
claims.relevance: Shows an adaptive inject-gate can avoid dropping below closed-book on easy items — the recall-floor protection our step-2-vs-step-1 comparison demands.

claims.claim: UAB (Uncertainty-Aware Budget) is a when-to-resample gate: per-question self-consistency variance drives greedy reallocation of a FIXED total sample budget T from low- to high-uncertainty questions, stopping when the hardest-easiest uncertainty gap falls below threshold; beats uniform allocation and sequential early-stopping on GPQA/MATH at equal cost.
claims.relevance: Operationalizes N* across items (not per-item) and reuses our best-of-N sample pool for the variance signal — a near-zero-marginal-cost budget gate.

claims.claim: UCCI shows the training-free dev-calibration recipe for a gate score: a raw token-margin is weak/miscalibrated, but a small ISOTONIC regression fit on a held-out calibration set turns it into a near-optimal probabilistic routing score; 'most cascade value comes from making the score probabilistic, not hand-tuning the final threshold.'
claims.relevance: Concrete, CPU-only, no-model-training calibration of tau* on our dev40 — the mechanically simplest way to convert any raw signal into a calibrated gate.

claims.claim: Conformal / selective-conformal gates (SCOPE, PASC, conformal risk control) calibrate the acceptance threshold on a dev calibration set so selective risk (error among answered) <= user alpha with finite-sample probability 1-delta, distribution-free. A separate RL-tuned variant (Learning Conformal Abstention Policies, 2502.06884) uses reinforcement learning and is comparison-class, not a training-free candidate.
claims.relevance: Gives tau* a guaranteed-coverage form tied to alpha; also cleanly separates the training-free conformal gate (candidate) from the RL-trained abstention policy (comparison-class).

claims.claim: SUGAR gates retrieval on context-based SEMANTIC entropy (cluster N sampled generations by meaning), which separates 'model truly lacks knowledge' from 'model uncertain about phrasing', and also chooses single-step vs multi-step retrieval depth.
claims.relevance: Meaning-level uncertainty is a stronger retrieve-gate signal than token entropy and reuses our best-of-N pool + CPU embedder; the single/multi-step choice hooks N*.

claims.claim: ClashEval documents the recall-floor risk quantitatively: even GPT-4 overrides its own CORRECT prior >60% of the time when given incorrect retrieved context. The bidirectional prior-biased vs context-biased error accounting, and follow-ups (Three Regimes of Context-Parametric Conflict 2605.11574; Task Matters 2506.06485), give a predictive framework for when injection helps vs harms.
claims.relevance: This is the empirical case for a prior-probability inject-gate as the mechanism that keeps step-2 mock from falling below step-1 closed-book.

claims.claim: SeaKR-style gates read INTERNAL states (Gram-matrix eigen-uncertainty of hidden layers) to decide retrieve, rerank snippets by uncertainty-reduction, and pick a reasoning strategy. This requires per-token hidden-state access that llama.cpp's llama-server does not expose, making the internal-state family infeasible on our GGUF resident-server stack without a different runtime.
claims.relevance: Prunes a whole popular gating family from our implementable set and explains WHY we must build gates from logprob-level signals (entropy/margin/two-pass contrastive), which llama-server does expose.

claims.claim: Adaptive-consistency/early-stopping gates (CGES Bayesian posterior-mass halt 2511.02603; RASC quality+consistency NAACL2025; Reliability-Aware 2601.02970; CITE anytime-valid confidence sequences 2605.05873) halt best-of-N once evidence suffices — up to ~7.9x fewer samples at <0.1% accuracy loss for the original Adaptive-Consistency.
claims.relevance: The when-to-resample stopping gate; near-zero marginal cost on top of our best-of-N; principled N* instantiation with validity guarantees (CITE).

claims.claim: Training-free confidence-elicitation gates that need no dev labels exist: P(True) self-evaluation (frozen model scores 'is the answer correct? yes/no', normalized yes-prob = confidence) and verbalized confidence, optionally fused with 2-sample consistency ('Two Samples Are Enough'). Models are often calibrated-in-confidence yet fail to convert it into an abstention policy — the fusion closes that adoption gap.
claims.relevance: Cheapest cross-model-verify gate on our stack (one extra short pass on the resident server); the calibrated-but-not-adopted finding maps directly to our alpha (adoption) term.

claims.claim: Retrieval-similarity is itself a deployable gate: empirical analyses show ~98.6% of off-topic retrievals score <0.7 cosine while ~89% of on-topic retrievals score >0.7, so a top-1 similarity threshold cleanly gates inject/skip; Adaptive-k (2506.08479) extends this to choose HOW MANY chunks to inject with no tuning and no iteration.
claims.relevance: The one natively-speech gate signal on our stack — faiss already returns the speech-keyed distance in p2, so this gate costs zero extra GPU and directly protects the recall floor.

candidates.name: TARG margin/entropy retrieval gate
candidates.what: Single-shot when-to-retrieve gate: from a k~20 draft prefix compute top1/top2 logit-gap margin (default), mean token entropy, or small-N prefix variance; retrieve iff U>tau. Calibrate tau on dev40 via empirical inverse-CDF to a target retrieval budget rho, or by max-dev-accuracy. No fusion (ablation showed single signal best).
candidates.cost: L. llama-server exposes top-k logprobs (n_probs) so margin/entropy come free from the answer's own prefix or one short draft; tau fit on dev40 is CPU-only. GPU: no extra memory, at most +1 short generation serialized on the resident server.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (threshold IS the gating radius; tau=F^{-1}(1-rho) is the dev calibration) + recall-floor (skips injection when unneeded) + alpha (retrieval rate rho = adoption)
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2511.09803v2 (WebFetch): Qwen2.5-7B NQ-Open 39.6 EM @30.4% retrieval vs 38.8 never/37.4 always; Llama-3.1-8B 57.6 EM @0.8% retrieval; 70-90% retrieval cut; usefulness-calibration Sec 3.3.

candidates.name: Multi-signal gate fusion (entropy+margin+consistency+retrieval-sim)
candidates.what: Fuse several cheap deployable signals — token entropy, top1/top2 margin, self-consistency/semantic-entropy, and faiss top-1 retrieval similarity — into one gate via a small logistic/weighted combiner calibrated on dev40. Motivated by the proof that no single signal is safe for selective prediction; directly contests TARG's single-signal finding on the speech-omni.
candidates.cost: M. Most signals reuse passes we already run (answer logits + best-of-N pool + faiss score); combiner fit on dev40 is CPU. GPU: no extra memory; marginal extra time only if semantic-entropy clustering is added.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (better gate radius) + tau (lower selector error) + alpha
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2603.21172 (WebFetch, entropy-alone-insufficient; AURC/E-AURC/AUROC protocol) vs arXiv 2511.09803v2 (TARG found no fusion gain) — the disagreement is the testable question.

candidates.name: CoCoA token-level context-vs-parametric inject gate
candidates.what: At each token compute Renyi(0.5) divergence between parametric p_theta (no retrieved context) and contextual p_theta^ctx, an entropy gap, and contextual peakedness; fuse into a conflict score and a blend weight lambda_t; emit q ∝ (p_ctx)^lambda (p_theta)^(1-lambda). Fixed hyperparameters, no per-task training. Preserves accuracy on low-conflict items.
candidates.cost: M. Needs TWO forward passes per generation (with/without retrieved context) plus token logprobs, both supported by llama-server. GPU: ~2x generation time on the resident server, no extra memory; the closed-book pass can reuse the step-1 run.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* + delta_corr (p_theta vs p_theta^ctx = two context-differentiated readings of the frozen omni, TH2a at token grain) + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2508.17670v2 (WebFetch, EMNLP2025): NQ-SWAP 80.8 (+18.0 over AdaCAD); NQ-SYNTH low-conflict 86.6 vs CAD 64.0 (-24.2 pt).

candidates.name: ClashEval-style prior-probability inject gate (item-level)
candidates.what: Item-level version of the contrastive gate: measure the frozen omni's answer probability WITHOUT context (prior) vs WITH context; if the prior is confident and disagrees with retrieval, down-weight or skip injection. Uses bidirectional prior-biased vs context-biased error accounting.
candidates.cost: M. Two passes per item (closed-book + open-book); the closed-book prior is exactly our step-1 baseline run, so marginal cost is one open-book pass already needed by the mock.
candidates.theory_hook: recall-floor (keeps mock from overriding a correct prior with bad retrieval = the step-2-vs-step-1 win) + tau* + delta_corr
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2404.10198 (ClashEval: GPT-4 overrides correct prior >60% under wrong context) + 2605.11574 (Three Regimes) + 2506.06485 (Task Matters) [snippets].

candidates.name: Retrieval-similarity necessity gate
candidates.what: Gate inject/skip on the faiss top-1 cosine/distance of the speech-keyed query; inject only if similarity>threshold (empirically ~0.7 separates in/out-of-domain), else fall back to closed-book. Pure retriever signal, no generation needed.
candidates.cost: L. The distance is already computed in the p2 KB lookup; threshold fit on dev40 is CPU-only. GPU: zero extra.
candidates.theory_hook: recall-floor (prevents injecting a wrong neighborhood) + tau* + alpha
candidates.evidence: RAG threshold analyses (98.6% off-topic <0.7 vs 89% on-topic >0.7) + TARG U>tau framing [snippets].

candidates.name: Adaptive-k context-quantity gate
candidates.what: Training-free rule to choose HOW MANY retrieved chunks to inject from the similarity-score distribution (gap/elbow), no tuning, no iteration; caps injected context to the useful set to avoid distraction.
candidates.cost: L. Operates on faiss scores already in p2; CPU only; no extra GPU.

candidates.name: SUGAR semantic-entropy retrieve + depth gate
candidates.what: Cluster N sampled generations by meaning (NLI/embedding) to get semantic entropy; gate whether to retrieve AND whether to go single-step vs multi-step. Meaning-invariant, separating true knowledge gaps from phrasing variance.
candidates.cost: M. Reuses the best-of-N sample pool; semantic clustering runs on the CPU embedder/NLI (GPU is held by llama-server). No extra GPU memory.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* + N* (single vs multi retrieval depth = budget)
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2501.04899 [snippet]: semantic-entropy gate improves QA and efficiency.

candidates.name: UAB uncertainty-aware resample-budget gate
candidates.what: Per-question self-consistency variance drives greedy reallocation of a FIXED total sample budget T from low- to high-uncertainty questions; stop when the hardest-easiest uncertainty gap drops below threshold. Turns a flat best-of-N into a difficulty-adaptive budget.
candidates.cost: M. Variance reuses the best-of-N pool; reallocation/stopping is CPU. GPU: same total generations, just redistributed across items.
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2605.26849 (WebFetch): beats uniform + sequential early-stop on GPQA/MATH at equal cost.

candidates.name: Adaptive-consistency / confidence-guided stopping gate
candidates.what: Halt best-of-N sampling once evidence suffices: CGES halts on Bayesian posterior mass over candidate answers; RASC uses reasoning-quality + answer-consistency criteria; CITE gives anytime-valid confidence-sequence stopping with no peeking penalty.
candidates.cost: L-M. Marginal on top of best-of-N; stopping rule is CPU. GPU: fewer generations than fixed-N on easy items (net saving).
candidates.theory_hook: N* (interior stopping = budget cap, CITE adds a validity guarantee) + tau
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2511.02603 CGES, 2408.17017 RASC (NAACL2025), 2601.02970, 2605.05873 CITE [snippets]; Adaptive-Consistency ~7.9x fewer samples, <0.1% acc loss.

candidates.name: UCCI isotonic dev-calibration of the gate score
candidates.what: Recipe, not a standalone gate: take any raw signal (token margin, entropy) and fit a small ISOTONIC regression on held-out dev40 to turn it into a calibrated probabilistic gate score, then threshold for cost-optimal deferral/abstention. 'Most value is making the score probabilistic, not tuning the threshold.'
candidates.cost: L. Isotonic fit + thresholding on dev40, CPU-only, no model training, no extra GPU. Wraps every other gate candidate.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (the training-free dev calibration of the gate radius) + tau + alpha
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2605.18796 UCCI [snippet]: isotonic on held-out set -> near-optimal routing score.

candidates.name: Conformal selective-prediction gate (SCOPE / risk-control)
candidates.what: Calibrate the acceptance threshold on a dev calibration set so selective risk (error among answered) <= user-specified alpha with finite-sample probability 1-delta, distribution-free. Gives tau* a guaranteed-coverage form and a risk-coverage curve for free.
candidates.cost: L. Calibration-set quantile on dev40, CPU-only, no GPU, no training.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* + alpha (user risk level = abstention/adoption target)
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2602.13110 SCOPE, 2605.18812 PASC [snippets]: risk <= alpha w.p. 1-delta.

candidates.name: P(True) / verbalized-confidence cross-verify gate
candidates.what: After generation, ask the frozen omni (different system prompt) 'Is the proposed answer correct? yes/no' and read the normalized yes-probability as confidence; gate/abstain/resample on it. Optionally fuse with 2-sample self-consistency ('Two Samples Are Enough') to convert known-but-unused confidence into an abstention policy.
candidates.cost: L. One extra short pass on the resident server (yes/no scoring); optional +1 sample. GPU: no extra memory, minor serialized time.
candidates.theory_hook: delta_corr (second context-differentiated pass of the frozen omni) + tau* + alpha (closes the calibrated-but-not-adopted gap)

candidates.name: Faithfulness / self-verification post-hoc gate
candidates.what: After generation, use the frozen omni as an evidence-grounding judge (answer-vs-retrieved-context); below a dev-calibrated threshold, fall back to closed-book / abstain / re-retrieve. A real-time faithfulness gate in the response path.
candidates.cost: M. One extra judge pass per item on the resident server; threshold on dev40. GPU: no extra memory.
candidates.theory_hook: delta_corr (generator vs verifier = two context-differentiated frozen systems, TH2a) + tau* + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2606.05644 FIDES + faithfulness-gate practice + our TH2a omni-verifier memo [snippets].

candidates.name: LLM-independent question-only retrieve gate
candidates.what: Predict retrieval need from features of the QUESTION alone (no LLM uncertainty), via a cheap external estimator robust to the choice of base model.
candidates.cost: L compute but requires a small labeled dev classifier (borderline training-free: external features, not model weights). CPU only, no GPU.
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2505.04253 'Let the Question Speak for Itself' [snippet].

candidates.name: LATTS step-level resample/backtrack gate
candidates.what: Step-level verifier score gates a per-reasoning-step decision to accept, resample, backtrack, or terminate — fine-grained resample gating inside a chain rather than at the whole-answer level.
candidates.cost: H. Needs a step-level verifier (our omni-as-verifier = extra passes per step) plus search bookkeeping; heavy on a single serialized GPU server. Best deferred to Stage-2.

candidates.name: SeaKR internal-state self-aware uncertainty gate
candidates.what: Read hidden-layer Gram-matrix eigen-uncertainty to gate retrieve, rerank snippets by uncertainty-reduction, and select a reasoning strategy. Powerful but requires per-token internal-state access.
candidates.cost: H / BLOCKED on our stack. llama.cpp llama-server does not expose hidden states; would need a different runtime (vLLM/HF) that OOMs on the 30B on our 5090. Documented as infeasible-on-stack, not a live candidate.
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2406.19215 [snippet] + stack constraint (no hidden-state API from GGUF server).

candidates.name: Learned conformal abstention policy (RL-tuned)
candidates.what: Uses reinforcement learning to optimize abstention/gating thresholds dynamically; reports +3.2% accuracy, +22% AUROC for hallucination detection. Included only as the comparison ceiling — it changes a policy via training and is out-of-scope for training-free.
candidates.cost: N/A (excluded). Requires RL training of a policy; violates the no-training constraint.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (as the trained-ceiling reference for our training-free tau* gates)

candidates.name: RAGate / TA-ARE trained gates
candidates.what: RAGate trains a gating model on human binary-augmentation judgments; TA-ARE replaces a static threshold with a learned time-aware estimator (-14.9% redundant retrievals). Both require supervised training of the gate.
candidates.cost: N/A (excluded). Needs labeled training of the gate; use only as an upper-reference for our training-free calibration.

gaps:
SPEECH-NATIVE GATING IS THIN: nearly all adaptive-gating work is text/VLM; the only audio-native signal I found is dLLM-ASR confidence-based early-exit and generic abstention. Transfer path to our omni is via (a) the text-token logprobs llama-server already exposes (entropy/margin/two-pass contrastive all work), and (b) the faiss speech-key distance (the one genuinely-audio gate). Whether paralinguistic/acoustic uncertainty adds a signal beyond text logprobs is unmeasured and is a Stage-2 question.

STACK CONSTRAINT PRUNES A WHOLE FAMILY: llama.cpp llama-server does not expose hidden states, so the SeaKR/internal-state/probing-classifier gating family (a large slice of the 2024-25 literature) is infeasible without switching runtimes (vLLM/HF OOM the 30B on the 5090). All implementable candidates must be built from logprob-level or retrieval-level signals — verify llama-server's n_probs/logprobs granularity (top-k depth, whether pre- or post-sampling) before committing.

TWO OPEN CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE ON OUR DATA (directional-only): (1) TARG found single-signal beats fusion, but the entropy-alone-insufficient proof says fusion is needed for SAFE selective prediction — resolvable only by measuring AURC on the speech-omni. (2) Self-consistency is reportedly losing its edge on modern models (arXiv 2511.00751 diminishing returns) — the resample-gate family (UAB/CGES/CITE) may show smaller gains on Qwen3-Omni-30B than on the 7-8B models in the papers.

VERIFICATION DEPTH: 4 candidates opened in full via WebFetch (TARG, CoCoA, Entropy-Alone-Insufficient, UAB) — their numbers/formulas are quoted. The remaining ~17 are from search-result snippets (title+abstract level); their mechanisms are reliable but exact numbers and dev-calibration details should be confirmed by fetching before Stage-2 pre-registration. Priority fetches for the freeze meeting: UCCI (2605.18796, the isotonic-calibration recipe), SUGAR (2501.04899), and SCOPE (2602.13110) for the conformal-alpha binding.

NOT RE-SURVEYED (per instruction, already in prior coverage): TARG is treated as a live candidate here because it is the direct tau* instantiation, but the TARG/Drozdov/Meta-k/NEST gating LINE, Beirami BoN bounds, HedgeTune/BoP N*, Weaver aggregation, and kNN-Whisper OOD harm are assumed held from earlier passes and only referenced as theory hooks, not re-derived.
